subject: EvCharge multi-cloud private offer — APAC carveouts and LATAM reseller routing
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Torres <liam.torres@evcharge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: EvCharge private offer — initial pricing notes

Liam,

Thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and the proposed starting point for the private offer that will cover deployments on AWS/GCP/Azure:

• Blended list price: we propose a single ratecard for core inference units (compute + model token units) with cloud-specific multipliers applied at invoice time.
• APAC carveout: separate regional line items to reflect higher infra + compliance costs (we've modelled a 8–12% regional uplift depending on country).
• LATAM reseller routing: we understand you want to route through your LATAM distributor for invoicing — Redwood will preserve list price and allocate a reseller netback allowance (TBD).

Attached: EVCharge_PO_Template.pdf (your procurement team asked for a formal PO format) and a draft ratecard (RDW-Ratecard-EVCharge-v2.xlsx) with example buckets.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Liam/Priya confirm whether the LATAM distributor will be named on the PO or if EvCharge will invoice centrally.
2) EvCharge to indicate any mandatory legal/PO language.
3) Redwood to publish a private-offer draft (DocuSign) once we lock reseller netback % and APAC uplift bands.

I've looped Ben (channel economics) and Irene (global pricing) to scope margin impacts.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior GTM Finance | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: EVCharge_PO_Template.pdf; RDW-Ratecard-EVCharge-v2.xlsx

From: Liam Torres <liam.torres@evcharge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@evcharge.com>, procurement@evcharge.com
Date: 2025-07-21T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EvCharge private offer — initial pricing notes

Hi Naomi,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from procurement and our LATAM partner side:

• LATAM routing: our LATAM distributor (MobilityLatam S.A.) needs to be on the invoice for local tax and import logistics. We prefer Redwood to bill MobilityLatam net of the reseller margin; they will issue local invoices to our country teams.
• Reseller margin expectation: MobilityLatam has asked for a 16% reseller margin as a starting point — they provide regional implementation and first-line support. Can you confirm Redwoods comfort with that level or suggest alternatives?
• APAC uplift: in SEA (Singapore/Thailand) we can accept an uplift range of 7–10%, but for Japan/Korea we expect a higher band (10–14%) due to data residency/ops costs.

I've attached our preferred PO language (we use the second clause set for private offers) and a short note from MobilityLatam about invoicing format.

We'd like to close commercial terms by end of next week if possible — our execs want a signed private offer ahead of our procurement review meeting on Aug 3.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships | EvCharge
liam.torres@evcharge.com
Attachment stubs: EvCharge_PO_Lang_v1.docx; MobilityLatam_InvoiceSpec.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Torres <liam.torres@evcharge.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-22T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EvCharge private offer — channel economics and reseller netback

Liam / Naomi,

Thanks for the detail — a couple concrete proposals from a channel margin perspective that should get us to a draft private offer quickly:

1) LATAM (MobilityLatam): propose a 15% reseller margin on list price with an additional implementation credit (one-time) to MobilityLatam to cover deployment in-country. We can make the implementation credit payable on acceptance of the first 3-month invoice. This keeps global economics predictable and reduces list-price leakage.

2) APAC uplift bands: agree to a tiered uplift on list price by country grouping — SEA: +8%, ANZ: +10%, JP/KR: +12%. These are applied as invoice multipliers, not changes to the core unit price.

3) Commitment buckets: if EvCharge commits to a 12-month reserved capacity (node-hours), we can offer a committed discount of 18% off list for the committed units (applies before reseller margin). This is additive to regional uplifts/invoice routing.

4) Legal/PO: we can accept MobilityLatam as the billed party provided the PO references Redwood deal id (RDW-DEAL-2025-0517-EVCH) and includes a reseller routing clause. Our standard procurement prefers the reseller to acknowledge responsibility for local taxes.

I've attached a quick ratecard example (same workbook Naomi shared) with sample math showing netback to MobilityLatam at 15% and the committed discount scenarios.

If that sounds OK, Naomi and I can produce a private-offer PDF + DocuSign envelope for EvCharge to sign. Budget-wise this keeps Redwood unit economics within our targeted thresholds for multi-cloud support.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: RDW-Ratecard-EVCharge-v2.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Torres <liam.torres@evcharge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, procurement@evcharge.com
Date: 2025-07-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EvCharge private offer — final commercial checks and timeline

Liam / Priya / MobilityLatam team,

Summary and next steps so we can hit your Aug 3 procurement meeting:

• LATAM: Redwood proposes 15% reseller margin to MobilityLatam + one-time implementation credit (payable after first 3-month invoice). If MobilityLatam can accept the 15% we will reflect this in the private offer and set MobilityLatam as the billed party.
• APAC: invoice multipliers — SEA +8%, ANZ +10%, JP/KR +12%. These are applied at invoicing and do not alter the committed discount math.
• Commitments: 12-month reserved capacity -> 18% committed discount on committed units (applies before reseller margin).

Please confirm all three items (reseller margin acceptance, wording for PO invoicing, and whether EvCharge will sign as primary or have MobilityLatam countersign) by EOD Tue Jul 29 so we can assemble the DocuSign and legal exhibits.

I'll ask Legal to add a short reseller-routing exhibit (one page) to the private offer; Ben will prepare the final ratecard numbers. Once we have confirmation, we'll send a DocuSign link and a final PO-ready PDF.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — 2 action items for EvCharge procurement: confirm MobilityLatam acceptance of 15% and indicate billing party preference.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior GTM Finance | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
